proposed_comments.title: Restore the cursor scheme only when Auto Hide Cursor owns it

confidence.rationale: The converged review fixes introduced a dedicated recovery marker and restoration guard specifically because the unfixed logic can clobber unrelated system-cursor state.

proposed_comments.body:
### Restore the cursor scheme only when Auto Hide Cursor owns it

**Severity:** `high`

The current implementation can reload the global system cursor scheme during disable or worker recovery even when this module did not leave the system cursors in the hidden state. That can overwrite another application's temporary cursor changes and makes crash recovery depend on mutable user files. Please track cursor ownership with a durable recovery marker and restore the scheme only when that marker proves Auto Hide Cursor actually replaced the system cursors.

proposed_comments.title: Reset worker backoff after stable runs and honor restarts promptly

confidence.rationale: The supervisor loop currently needs both a stable-lifetime reset and a restart-aware retry wait to avoid minute-long delays after unrelated failures.

proposed_comments.body:
### Reset worker backoff after stable runs and honor restarts promptly

**Severity:** `medium`

The worker retry counter currently keeps accumulating across unrelated failures, so ordinary long-lived runs can still end up stuck behind minute-long restart delays later. In the same area, retry sleep should also wake immediately for a settings-triggered restart instead of waiting out the failure delay. Please treat only rapid consecutive failures as a crash loop and let restart signals interrupt the backoff wait.

proposed_comments.title: Keep Auto Hide Cursor settings normalized across parsing, persistence, and UI

confidence.rationale: This PR adds new persisted settings and multiple load paths; the review fixes had to add invalid-type handling and normalized-delay assertions to keep runtime and UI behavior aligned.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep Auto Hide Cursor settings normalized across parsing, persistence, and UI

**Severity:** `medium`

This feature introduces a new persisted idle-delay setting and multiple settings-entry points, so malformed JSON types or out-of-range values can otherwise leave the runtime and Settings UI disagreeing about the effective configuration. Please normalize the persisted values at load time, clamp invalid delay values consistently, and make the UI/tests assert the normalized behavior rather than the raw file contents.

proposed_comments.title: Cover worker cleanup and recovery with authoritative UI assertions

confidence.rationale: The delayed follow-up review produced a concrete test-reliability finding, and the converged fix replaced fragile handle-based assertions with recovery-marker checks and stale-worker cleanup.

proposed_comments.body:
### Cover worker cleanup and recovery with authoritative UI assertions

**Severity:** `medium`

The new UI tests need to start from a clean worker state and verify recovery with an authoritative signal. Please include the Auto Hide Cursor worker in the stale-process cleanup list, and validate hide/restore and crash recovery with the recovery marker (or rendered cursor pixels) instead of assuming `HCURSOR` handles change when `SetSystemCursor` swaps the underlying cursor contents.
